What each province's statute says: 22 coded rules and the model-statute indices

Source: group coding of the 24 provincial teacher statutes (qualitative_codebook.xlsx), primary grade teacher unless stated. Index cells: 0–100, darker = closer to the model statute. Rule cells: shaded by the same 0–1 score (darker = closer to the model statute; plain = direction not set or not in the indices); ● = yes, ○ = no, – = not coded. Click a row to select the province, a column heading to map that rule.

How the indices are built

Each rule is rescaled to 0–1 across provinces (yes/no rules as they are; numbers from the lowest to the highest province), flipped where a lower value is closer to the model statute, and averaged within its dimension (missing codes skipped). Dimension index = 100 × that average; overall index = average of the four dimensions. A rule enters the indices only if the direction is clear and it varies: at least 3 provinces differ from the most common value and at least 16 of 24 are coded. Directions are set in 2_do/statute_index_spec.csv; edit it and rerun scripts 10 and 09 to change them.

Teaching workforce, posts and pay

Sources and definitions

Aprender national assessment microdata (Ministry of Education), cleaned in Stata by the project pipeline (1_data/2_do). Outcomes are weighted with each subject's expansion weight. Levels: satisfactory or advanced = levels 3–4 of 4. Cut scores are identical across 2018–2025.

Caveats. 2021 grade 6: the microdata gives much higher language results (70.9%) than the original official report (56%); treat 2021 as unresolved. 2022 grade 6 is a sample, not a census. Secondary results compare 2016 with 2024 only. Socioeconomic groups use each cycle's own scheme (three levels before 2024/25, quintiles after): "top" and "bottom" are the extreme groups of that scheme, so SES gaps are not comparable across those years. Scores are not comparable across levels.

Workforce. Shares of teachers or directors who answered each question (census questionnaires); these are not staffing counts, and teacher answers describe the school, not a particular pupil's teacher. 2025 hours items: the teacher codebook labels are shifted by one; we read code 1 as "does not work there" (consistent with the director codebook). Associations in the scatter are descriptive, not causal.

Posts & pay. Relevamiento Anual (annual school census, 2011–2025): teaching posts (cargos) and teaching hours (horas cátedra + módulos) in front of students, by status in the planta funcional. Substitutes are counted separately (per 100 planta). Pupils per post: primary only, common-education enrolment / filled teaching posts. CGECSE salaries 2003–2026, quarterly, nominal pesos.

SES-expected results. For each province, the expected satisfactory share is what the province would score if each of its SES groups (bottom, middle, top) scored like that group nationally, weighting by the province's own SES mix (unweighted counts of tested students with SES data). Above zero = the province does better than its intake predicts. Indirect standardisation; it ignores other intake differences.

Teacher traits vs school results. 2025 grade-6 schools with 10+ tested students, linked to their own responding teachers. Coefficient = difference in the school's satisfactory share (pts) between a school where all and none of the responding teachers have the trait. Model 2 adds the school's SES mix, sector and area; model 3 adds province fixed effects (compares schools within the same province). Weighted by tested students, robust SEs. Associations, not causal effects: teachers sort across schools.

Benchmarks. ERCE 2019 and PISA estimates use all plausible values with Fay-BRR replicate weights and pass the official benchmark checks (pipeline stages 01, 04, 06). MICS 2019–20 (UNICEF) urban sample, design-based CIs (stage 05). OECD averages are typed in from published reports.

Compare tab. Splits provinces into four groups at the Argentina value (or median) of each indicator. It describes co-occurrence across 24 provinces only.

Statute rules. The group coded the 24 provincial teacher statutes on 22 rules in four dimensions (qualitative_codebook.xlsx; reference post: primary grade teacher). Script 10_statute_coding.py turns them into a 0–100 model-statute index per dimension and overall (method in the Statute rules tab; directions in 2_do/statute_index_spec.csv). The outcome tabs show a statute map next to each outcome map and a table of one-at-a-time regressions across provinces: R² is the share of cross-province differences a statute measure accounts for; the SES columns hold constant the share of grade-6 pupils in the lowest SES group (Aprender 2025) and report the partial R². With at most 24 provinces these are descriptive associations: they cannot separate the law from everything else that differs between provinces, and the codes describe the statute as written now, not its history or enforcement.
